newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian minister hopes for labour deal by Xmas.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister hopes for labour deal by Xmas.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Wednesday he hoped employers and trades unions could end a bitter dispute over a pay settlement for 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers by Christmas.
Treu has scheduled separate talks on Thursday with employers group Federmeccanica and the three unions, FIOM, FIM and UILM, to try to end months of deadlock.

"I hope there will be a contract by Christmas," Treu told reporters. "I hope everyone will show a will to proceed though it is going to take a few days to understand how the situation is going to develop."
Union-employer contracts expired in June. The unions recently held two eight-hour strikes and have threatened further stoppages if Federmeccanica does not meet their pay demands.
The unions want management to compensate workers in full for higher-than-expected inflation in the past contractual period.

In cash terms, unions want a gross 262,000 lire ($171) rise in monthly pay packets, of which 97,000 is to cover the overrun in inflation between 1994 and 1996. Employers have offered 195,000 lire of which 30,000 is for inflation. ($1=1533 Lire)
